hero.headline: U.S. and Iran reach tentative ceasefire extension deal pending Trump approval
hero.body:
U.S. and Iranian negotiators have reached a tentative agreement to extend a ceasefire for 60 days and begin new nuclear talks, according to U.S. officials. The deal now awaits final approval from President Trump.

Trump unilaterally announced the ceasefire extension on Tuesday through his Truth Social platform after hours of escalating rhetoric in which he said he "expected to be bombing." The extension came after requests from Pakistani leaders to hold military action while Iranian negotiators work toward a unified proposal.

"Based on the fact that the Government of Iran is seriously fractured, not unexpectedly so and, upon the request of Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, of Pakistan, we have been asked to hold our Attack on the Country of Iran until such time as their leaders and representatives can come up with a unified proposal," Trump wrote.

The agreement would extend the existing ceasefire for two months and create a framework for renewed negotiations on Iran's nuclear program. The tentative deal represents a potential diplomatic breakthrough after years of heightened tensions between Washington and Tehran.

However, Iran has sent conflicting signals about the negotiations. Tehran's state television broadcast a message confirming that no Iranian delegation had visited Islamabad for talks. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the speaker of Iran's parliament and the regime's lead negotiator, dismissed the ceasefire extension as "a ploy to buy time for a surprise strike." His personal adviser Mahdi Mohammadi said on social media that Iran must take military initiative, stating "the losing side cannot dictate terms."

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who has served as principal mediator, thanked Trump and said Pakistan would continue efforts for a negotiated settlement.

A major obstacle remains the ongoing U.S. Navy blockade of Iranian ports. Iran has insisted the blockade must end before negotiations resume. However, Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent both warned on Tuesday that the blockade will continue. Bessent stated that Iranian oil storage on Kharg Island will be full within days, threatening to shut in fragile Iranian wells.

U.S. forces have escalated pressure through the blockade by seizing Iranian cargo vessels and boarding oil tankers previously sanctioned for smuggling Iranian crude oil. Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei characterized these actions as "piracy at sea and state terrorism."

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iran, announced early in the conflict, has cut off supply of approximately one-fifth of the world's oil and gas. The International Energy Agency's chief called the combined impact of the conflict on energy markets "the biggest crisis in history."

The White House has not issued a public statement on whether Trump will approve the tentative deal.

cards.headline: Netanyahu orders Israeli forces to expand control to 70% of Gaza Strip
cards.teaser: The Israeli prime minister directed the military to seize a larger portion of Gaza, violating ceasefire terms.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has directed the Israeli military to seize control of 70 percent of the Gaza Strip, according to reports from The Guardian and CNN. This expansion of Israeli forces contradicts the terms of the existing ceasefire agreement, which restricts military operations in the territory.

The directive marks a significant escalation in Gaza operations. Meanwhile, a separate Israeli strike in Gaza City killed Mohammed Odeh, the newly appointed head of Hamas's military wing, along with his wife and two children in an attack on a residential building, according to Hamas.

cards.headline: Israel conducts targeted strike on Beirut as tensions rise with Hezbollah
cards.teaser: The Lebanese capital had largely avoided strikes even as both sides accused each other of breaking last month's ceasefire.
cards.body:
Israel carried out a targeted strike on Beirut, marking a significant escalation in the Lebanese capital. The city had largely avoided attacks throughout the conflict until this operation.

Both Israel and Hezbollah have accused each other of violating the ceasefire agreement reached last month. The strike represents a departure from the relative calm Beirut had maintained during the broader conflict.

cards.headline: U.S. Central Command says Iranian attack on Kuwait violated ceasefire
cards.teaser: The military called the strike an egregious violation as both sides trade accusations.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian negotiators are working toward extending their ceasefire and reaching a broader agreement. U.S. officials say they are closing in on preliminary terms, though President Trump has not yet signed off on the emerging framework. Key negotiations are focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, where significant sticking points remain.

Despite diplomatic progress, both sides have continued trading strikes and accusations. U.S. Central Command characterized the Iranian attack on Kuwait as an egregious violation of the fragile truce between the two countries.

cards.headline: Trump administration opens Ebola quarantine facility in Kenya for exposed Americans
cards.teaser: A 50-bed field hospital in Kenya will house Americans exposed to Ebola, with no plans to allow them back into the United States.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is establishing a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola during the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rather than allowing them to return to the United States. The 50-bed field hospital will become operational Friday.

The policy shift has drawn criticism from some experts, who argue that preventing Americans from returning home may hinder treatment efforts.

cards.headline: California Governor Newsom announces plan to impose 100% tax on Trump's $1.8 billion fund
cards.teaser: Governor Gavin Newsom said California will impose a 100% tax on California recipients of payments from Trump's Anti-Weaponization Fund.
cards.body:
California Governor Gavin Newsom announced the state will impose a 100% tax on payments made to California residents from President Trump's $1.8 billion fund. The fund, which Trump has called the Anti-Weaponization Fund, was established in connection with January 6 events.

New York has also proposed legislation that would tax state residents who receive payments from the fund at 100%. The proposed state taxes would effectively nullify any payments to recipients in those jurisdictions.

cards.headline: Supreme Court allows Mississippi death row inmate to challenge exclusion of Black jurors
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled that a Mississippi man on death row can challenge the exclusion of Black jurors from his trial.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled in favor of a Mississippi death row inmate seeking to challenge whether Black jurors were improperly excluded from his trial. Justice Brett Kavanaugh authored the opinion, allowing the inmate to pursue claims of racial bias during jury selection.

The decision addresses persistent concerns about racial discrimination in how jurors are chosen in capital cases.

cards.headline: Austrian man sentenced to 15 years for plotting Taylor Swift concert attack in Vienna
cards.teaser: A 21-year-old was found guilty of planning the attack and other terrorism-related offenses.
cards.body:
A 21-year-old Austrian man has been sentenced to 15 years in prison after being found guilty of plotting an attack on a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. The court convicted him of planning the attack along with other terrorism-related offenses.

The man was arrested before he could carry out the planned assault on the concert venue in the Austrian capital.

cards.headline: Guatemala agrees to joint U.S. operations targeting drug gangs
cards.teaser: The deal expands the Trump administration's campaign to press Latin American countries into allowing operations inside their borders.
cards.body:
Guatemala agreed to conduct joint strikes with the United States against drug gangs operating within its territory. The agreement allows American forces to participate in operations on Guatemalan soil.

The deal forms part of a broader Trump administration effort to secure agreements with Latin American countries for joint operations inside their borders. The administration has been pressing multiple countries in the region to accept similar arrangements for combating drug trafficking organizations.

cards.headline: Portugal sets new May temperature record as European heatwave intensifies
cards.teaser: France and Italy have issued alerts as extreme temperatures grip the continent.
cards.body:
Portugal broke its record for the hottest temperature ever recorded in May as a heatwave swept across Europe. The new record marks an unusual early-season spike in temperatures across the continent.

French students are taking their exams in sweltering school buildings as the heat affects daily life. Italy has issued red alerts in response to the extreme temperatures blanketing southern Europe.

cards.headline: Canadian Prime Minister Carney calls for new relationship with U.S. in New York speech
cards.teaser: Speaking in New York, the Canadian leader said distancing between the two countries benefits the United States.
cards.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney delivered a speech in New York calling for a new partnership between Canada and the United States. He emphasized the need for a "true partnership" that reimagines economic cooperation in sectors facing global competition.

Carney's remarks reflect Canada's effort to strengthen ties with its southern neighbor through enhanced collaboration and shared economic goals.

cards.body:

cards.headline: Former CIA official arrested after FBI finds $40 million in gold bars at his home
cards.teaser: Federal authorities arrested a former CIA official after discovering gold bars worth approximately $40 million inside his residence.
cards.body:
David Rush, a former senior CIA officer, has been arrested and faces charges of theft and making false statements. The FBI discovered a substantial cache of gold bars and millions in cash at his Virginia home during an operation. According to prosecutors, the precious metals and money had gone missing from Rush's CIA storage space.

The arrest followed the FBI's investigation into the missing valuables, which were reportedly worth approximately $40 million. The discovery at Rush's residence led to charges related to the alleged theft from the agency.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into nonprofit that funded E. Jean Carroll's legal costs
cards.teaser: The Justice Department has launched a criminal probe into a Democratic-allied nonprofit organization that helped pay legal bills for E. Jean Carroll.
cards.body:
The Justice Department has launched a criminal investigation into a nonprofit organization that provided financial support for E. Jean Carroll's civil lawsuits against President Trump. Carroll won her civil cases against Trump, and the nonprofit has ties to Democratic causes.

The investigation centers on whether Carroll made false statements regarding the funding she received for her litigation. This probe represents a new development following the conclusion of the legal battles between Carroll and Trump.

cards.headline: California Governor Newsom announces plan to impose 100% tax on Trump's $1.8 billion fund
cards.teaser: Governor Gavin Newsom said California will impose a 100% tax on California recipients of payments from Trump's Anti-Weaponization Fund.
cards.body:
California Governor Gavin Newsom announced the state will impose a 100% tax on payments made to California residents from President Trump's $1.8 billion fund. The fund, which Trump has called the Anti-Weaponization Fund, was established in connection with January 6 events.

New York has also proposed legislation that would tax state residents who receive payments from the fund at 100%. The proposed state taxes would effectively nullify any payments to recipients in those jurisdictions.

cards.headline: Treasury Department proposes $250 bill featuring Trump's image
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department is preparing a $250 bill that would feature President Trump's face, though Congress must pass legislation to authorize printing.
cards.body:
The White House is pursuing congressional approval for a $250 banknote bearing President Trump's portrait. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the proposal at a White House news conference, framing it as a celebration of the nation's 250th anniversary of independence. The Treasury Department has already begun preparations for the potential new currency.

The proposal would require changing federal law, which currently prohibits living individuals from appearing on US currency. Democrats have signaled opposition to the measure, with House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries telling Trump to "get over yourself" in response to the proposal.

cards.headline: Supreme Court allows Mississippi death row inmate to challenge exclusion of Black jurors
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled that a Mississippi man on death row can challenge the exclusion of Black jurors from his trial.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled in favor of a Mississippi death row inmate seeking to challenge whether Black jurors were improperly excluded from his trial. Justice Brett Kavanaugh authored the opinion, allowing the inmate to pursue claims of racial bias during jury selection.

The decision addresses persistent concerns about racial discrimination in how jurors are chosen in capital cases.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer announces she will not run for president in 2028
cards.teaser: Democratic Governor Gretchen Whitmer said she will not seek the presidency in 2028, closing the door on speculation about her potential candidacy.
cards.body:
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced she will not run for president in 2028. The Democratic governor's decision ends months of speculation about whether she would enter the next presidential race.

Whitmer has been considered a top potential Democratic candidate for the 2028 election. Her announcement removes one of the party's most prominent figures from consideration for the nomination.

hero.headline: Anthropic Surpasses OpenAI as Most Valuable AI Startup
hero.body:
Anthropic has become the world's most valuable artificial intelligence startup after raising $65 billion in Series H funding at a post-money valuation of $965 billion. The funding round, led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital, eclipses OpenAI's previous valuation of $852 billion, marking a significant shift in the competitive landscape of the AI industry.

The company's rapid ascent reflects the widespread adoption of Claude, its AI chatbot, particularly among large enterprise customers. The release of powerful coding assistants in recent months has strengthened Anthropic's position as a dominant player in the global AI market. Krishna Rao, the company's chief financial officer, stated that "Claude is increasingly indispensable to our growing global community of customers, and we work tirelessly to make tools like Claude Code and Cowork more helpful, more powerful, and more adaptable to their needs."

Anthropic's strategy has diverged from some competitors in several key ways. The company has focused heavily on enterprise and coding services rather than consumer-facing products. Additionally, Anthropic has positioned itself as prioritizing AI safety and responsible development. One of its co-founders attended a recent papal encyclical addressing dangers associated with AI technology. The company has also maintained legal disputes with the Pentagon, refusing to remove safeguards from Claude that would allow its use for mass domestic surveillance or lethal autonomous weapons systems.

This valuation milestone places Anthropic within striking distance of the $1 trillion threshold, a benchmark historically associated only with publicly traded technology giants. The company joins an extremely small group of private enterprises approaching such valuations.

The funding round underscores the enormous capital flows continuing into the AI sector despite public concerns about the technology. Anthropic's valuation surge follows OpenAI's $122 billion funding round in March, which valued that company at $852 billion. OpenAI is reportedly planning to pursue a $1 trillion initial public offering later this year.

Anthropic has also emerged as an influential force in policy discussions surrounding AI regulation. The company has advocated for increased government oversight of artificial intelligence technology, positioning itself differently from other industry leaders who favor lighter regulatory frameworks.

The deal demonstrates investor confidence in Anthropic's business model and technological capabilities. The company's focus on enterprise applications, combined with its public commitment to safety-conscious AI development, appears to have resonated with major capital providers. As competition intensifies among AI companies seeking to develop and commercialize advanced systems, Anthropic's latest valuation reflects the broader trend of substantial investment flowing toward leading AI firms.

cards.headline: ABC Accuses FCC of Threatening Broadcast Licenses
cards.teaser: The television network accused the Federal Communications Commission of targeting its station licenses in what it called unconstitutional retaliation.
cards.body:
ABC accused the Federal Communications Commission of threatening its broadcast licenses. The network said the FCC was conducting a campaign of unconstitutional retaliation against it.

Disney's ABC filed for early broadcast license renewals under protest against the FCC. The network characterized the actions as an assault on its television licenses. FCC Chair Brendan Carr moved up the expiration date of ABC television station licenses, prompting the network's response.

cards.headline: Treasury Prepares Trump for New $250 Bill
cards.teaser: Treasury Secretary Bessent supported placing Trump on a new $250 bill, which would require legislation to allow a living person on currency.
cards.body:
The White House is pushing Congress to approve a $250 bill featuring Donald Trump's portrait, according to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The administration frames the currency as a celebration of the country's 250th anniversary of independence, and the Treasury has already begun preparing for the possibility.

Federal law currently prohibits placing living persons on U.S. currency, so the proposal would require Congressional approval and a change to longstanding law. Trump allies in Congress are moving to make an exception, though Democrats have vowed to block the measure.

cards.headline: Trump Accounts App Launches to Manage $1,000 Federal Investment
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department rolled out an app to track a $1,000 federal investment given to newborns in the United States.
cards.body:
The Treasury Department has rolled out the Trump Accounts app nationwide, enabling families to track a $1,000 federal investment allocated to each child. Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the application's launch to help monitor these funds.

The app allows parents and guardians to manage the federal investment provided to newborns and children across the country.

cards.headline: Bari Weiss Names Nick Bilton to Lead 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: CBS editor in chief Bari Weiss appointed tech journalist Nick Bilton as executive producer of 60 Minutes and fired two on-air correspondents.
cards.body:
Bari Weiss, CBS News editor in chief, appointed Nick Bilton, a former New York Times technology journalist, as executive producer of 60 Minutes for the show's 59th season beginning in the fall. Bilton replaces Tanya Simon, who was ousted from the role.

The shake-up also included the non-renewal of veteran correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi's contract. Alfonsi has accused CBS News of penalizing her for refusing to alter factually accurate reporting, citing Weiss's decision to shelve a segment she reported on a prison in El Salvador.

cards.headline: Two Newspapers Named Star Launch in Washington
cards.teaser: The Star and The Washington Star both launched to compete for readers following recent layoffs at The Washington Post.
cards.body:
Two new newspapers called The Star and The Washington Star launched in Washington, D.C. Both publications aim to attract readers following recent layoffs at The Washington Post.

The Star was established first, followed by the rebirth of The Washington Star. The two papers are competing to win over readers who may be seeking alternatives after staff reductions at the Post.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Reach New Records on Tech Rally
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at new record highs, driven by technology stocks and corporate earnings.
cards.body:
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached new record highs as technology stocks rallied. Wall Street pushed to fresh records as profits continued to accumulate for U.S. companies.

Dell surged on earnings results, contributing to the technology sector's gains. Investors reacted positively to corporate profit reports, lifting major indexes to new peaks. The Dow Jones also rose alongside hopes for progress on Middle East negotiations.

hero.headline: Anthropic raises $65 billion at $965 billion valuation ahead of IPO
hero.body:
Anthropic has closed a $65 billion Series H funding round at a post-money valuation of $965 billion, bringing the artificial intelligence startup close to a trillion-dollar valuation. The company indicated this could be its final private fundraise before going public.

The funding round positions Anthropic among the most valuable private technology companies globally. The startup develops Claude, an AI assistant that competes with offerings from OpenAI and other major technology firms.

The $965 billion valuation represents a significant milestone for the AI sector, which has seen substantial investor interest over the past two years. Anthropic has raised multiple funding rounds as it develops and deploys large language models for enterprise and consumer applications.

The company suggested it is preparing for an initial public offering, which would make it one of the largest tech IPOs in recent years. An IPO would provide liquidity to early investors and employees while giving Anthropic access to public capital markets.

Anthropic was founded by former OpenAI executives who left to create what they described as a more safety-focused approach to AI development. The company has emphasized constitutional AI and other techniques aimed at making AI systems more reliable and aligned with human values.

The Series H round follows a pattern of escalating valuations in the AI sector, where companies developing foundational models have attracted substantial investment from venture capital firms, technology companies, and other institutional investors. The funding will support continued development of AI models and expansion of computing infrastructure.

The timing of the fundraise and IPO preparation comes as AI companies face growing demand from enterprises seeking to integrate AI capabilities into their operations. Anthropic competes in a market that includes well-funded rivals and established technology giants investing heavily in AI development.

cards.headline: FBI says Google engineer used internal search data to win $1.2 million on Polymarket
cards.teaser: Federal investigators say a Google employee used advance knowledge of search outcomes to profit on prediction markets.
cards.body:
The US Department of Justice has charged Michele Spagnuolo, a 36-year-old Google software engineer, with using insider information to place bets on Polymarket. According to prosecutors, Spagnuolo exploited access to Google's internal search data to predict outcomes and earned $1.2 million in profits from the prediction market platform.

Spagnuolo allegedly used confidential information about Google's most-searched list to place bets on long-shot candidates with advance knowledge of results. His arrest follows a similar case against a US Army soldier charged with using classified military information to make Polymarket bets about Venezuela.

cards.headline: Hackers target Signal users with phishing attacks aimed at backup access
cards.teaser: A new campaign attempts to trick users into revealing secret recovery keys that unlock message backups.
cards.body:
Hackers are conducting a phishing campaign targeting Signal users to steal their secret recovery keys. These keys grant access to online backups containing users' message history.

The attacks exploit social engineering rather than attempting to compromise Signal's encryption directly. Users who fall victim and share their recovery keys would expose their stored messages to attackers.

cards.headline: Cloud providers redesign infrastructure for machine-generated internet traffic
cards.teaser: AWS, Cloudflare, and others are rebuilding systems as AI agents move from testing to production use.
cards.body:
Major cloud infrastructure providers including AWS and Cloudflare are redesigning their systems as AI agents move from experimental deployments into production environments. This shift reflects expectations that machines will generate the majority of internet traffic in the future, rather than human users.

The transition requires fundamental changes to how cloud infrastructure operates, as machine-generated traffic creates different patterns and resource demands than traditional human web browsing and application usage.

cards.headline: Developer hides data-deletion prompt in code to target AI coding agents
cards.teaser: A programmer inserted hidden instructions telling AI tools to delete application output.
cards.body:
A developer added an undisclosed prompt injection into the jqwik codebase that instructed AI coding agents to delete application output. The insertion targeted what the developer described as vibe coders who rely heavily on AI assistance.

Prompt injection attacks exploit how AI systems process instructions embedded in data or code. By hiding commands within legitimate-looking code, the developer created a trap for AI agents that would execute the deletion instructions without human oversight.

cards.headline: Fine-tuned language models represent false statements as true despite warnings
cards.teaser: Testing shows AI systems display bias toward confidently stating claims even after being told they are false.
cards.body:
Research on fine-tuned large language models found they continue to represent false statements as true even after receiving explicit warnings about their falsity. Testing revealed a bias toward confidently presenting claims as accurate regardless of prior corrections.

The findings raise concerns about AI reliability and the difficulty of correcting misinformation once models have been trained. The research suggests that simply telling AI systems that information is false may not prevent them from later presenting that information as factual.

cards.headline: Asana acquires no-code AI agent builder StackAI
cards.teaser: The project management company will integrate StackAI into its AI workflow tools.
cards.body:
Asana has acquired StackAI, a no-code platform for building AI agents. The company plans to incorporate StackAI into its expanding suite of AI-powered workflow tools.

The acquisition adds agent-building capabilities to Asana's project management platform. StackAI allows users to create AI agents without writing code, making automation accessible to non-technical team members.

hero.headline: Four-time Stanley Cup champion Claude Lemieux dies at 60
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion known for his fierce, hard-hitting style of play, has died at age 60. According to the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, deputies responded to a furniture store showroom in Lake Park, Florida just after 3 a.m. Thursday where Lemieux was found. The sheriff's office confirmed the death was an apparent suicide.

Lemieux's playing style combined physical aggression with clutch performance in critical moments. His ferocious approach sometimes drew criticism from opponents and overshadowed his considerable skills, but his ability to elevate his game during playoff runs made him one of the sport's most decorated players.

During his NHL career, Lemieux won Stanley Cups with three different franchises. He captured championships with the Montreal Canadiens, the New Jersey Devils twice, and the Colorado Avalanche. His four championship rings place him among an elite group of players who achieved this level of success across multiple organizations.

Lemieux earned the Conn Smythe Trophy, awarded to the playoff MVP, in 1995. His reputation as an agitator who thrived under pressure made him a valuable asset during championship runs, though his competitive fire sometimes created friction with other players.

The discovery of Lemieux's death came through his family. His son found him at the family's furniture store business, which had become his focus following his playing career. Beyond his time on the ice, Lemieux later worked as a player agent.

Just days before his death, Lemieux had participated in a ceremonial role at the Eastern Conference finals, carrying the torch as part of the playoff festivities. This appearance stood in sharp contrast to the tragic news that followed shortly after.

The hockey community has expressed shock and sadness at Lemieux's passing. His contributions to the sport spanned more than two decades across multiple teams, establishing him as a respected and accomplished figure throughout the league.

Lemieux entered professional hockey with a distinctive style that made him memorable to fans and opponents alike. His nicknames reflected his personality and approach to the game, capturing both his intensity and his willingness to engage in confrontation. Yet beneath the physical play lay a player who understood how to perform when championships were on the line.

The loss of Lemieux represents a significant moment for the NHL community. His four Stanley Cup victories, achieved across different eras and teams, demonstrated a career of sustained excellence at hockey's highest level. The circumstances of his death have prompted reflection within the sports world about mental health and the pressures faced by athletes both during and after their playing careers.

cards.headline: MLB proposes hard salary cap in first offer to players union
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball has made its first proposal in collective bargaining negotiations, introducing details of a hard salary cap.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball submitted its initial offer to the players union, including a detailed proposal for a hard salary cap. The proposal marks the first time owners have pushed for a salary cap since the 1994-95 strike that canceled the World Series.

Eight MLB teams would need to reduce their current payroll under the proposed cap structure. The league framed the proposal as addressing competitive balance issues across the sport. The MLBPA has made its first counter-proposal in the ongoing collective bargaining negotiations.

cards.headline: Luke Littler wins Premier League darts title in 11-10 final over Luke Humphries
cards.teaser: World champion Luke Littler defeated Luke Humphries 11-10 to regain the Premier League darts title.
cards.body:
World champion Luke Littler claimed revenge against Luke Humphries to regain the Premier League darts title. Littler's 11-10 victory in the final showcased one of his finest performances and is being regarded as one of the competition's greatest matches.

The narrow win saw Littler edge out Humphries in a closely fought contest between two of the sport's top players.

cards.headline: NBA owners vote to expand draft lottery and pass anti-tanking rules
cards.teaser: The NBA Board of Governors has approved changes to the draft lottery and new rules designed to prevent tanking.
cards.body:
NBA team owners voted in favor of expanding the draft lottery and implementing measures to address tanking. The Board of Governors passed a new 3-2-1 format for the lottery system aimed at discouraging teams from losing intentionally.

The reform represents a significant change to how the NBA draft lottery operates. Some of the league's best teams are expected to benefit from the new system, which alters the incentive structure teams face when building their rosters.

cards.headline: Anderson Silva says he saved UFC more than once in response to Dana White
cards.teaser: Former UFC champion Anderson Silva has responded to Dana White's comments about their relationship after his UFC exit.
cards.body:
Anderson Silva fired back at UFC president Dana White over his departure from the promotion, claiming he saved the UFC more than once during his time with the organization.

White recently stated that Silva still refuses to speak with him, saying the UFC legend felt disrespected during his final stint. Silva has maintained his silence since leaving the promotion despite White's public comments about their relationship.

cards.headline: Jannik Sinner exits French Open early, opening men's draw
cards.teaser: Top player Jannik Sinner has been eliminated early from the French Open, opening up the men's tournament.
cards.body:
Jannik Sinner's second-round exit from the French Open has opened up the men's tournament. The world No. 1 suffered a heavy defeat to Argentina's Juan Manuel Cerúndolo, losing 3-6, 2-6, 7-5, 6-1, 6-1. Sinner attributed his loss to illness rather than the extreme heat at Roland Garros, describing the result as "tough to accept" given his recent form.

With Sinner sidelined, Alexander Zverev has emerged as the new favorite for the men's title. The Italian plans to skip grass-court tournaments and take time to recover before Wimbledon, indicating the extent of his physical and mental fatigue from the tournament.

cards.headline: India defeats England by 38 runs in opening T20 match
cards.teaser: England suffered a 38-run defeat to India in the first T20 match at Chelmsford.
cards.body:
India secured a commanding 38-run victory over England in the opening women's T20 international at Chelmsford. A partnership of 126 runs between Jemimah Rodrigues and Yastika Bhatia for the third wicket proved decisive in setting up India's winning total.

England's performance fell short throughout the match, with erratic displays both with bat and ball contributing to their defeat in the series opener.

hero.headline: CBS News Replaces 60 Minutes Executive Producer, Fires Several Correspondents
hero.body:
CBS News replaced the executive producer at 60 Minutes and fired several correspondents in a major reorganization announced Thursday. Bari Weiss, who leads CBS News, appointed Nick Bilton as the new leader of the program.

Cecilia Vega, one of the ousted correspondents, said she is worried about the future of the program under the management installed by parent company Paramount Skydance. She expressed respect and admiration for her colleagues at 60 Minutes.

Bilton said he wants the newsmagazine to be more prevalent in popular culture and the news cycle, rather than appearing only on Sunday evenings. He noted the show is on the air one day, one night, one hour a week.

Weiss called for a new approach to the long-running program. Sharyn Alfonsi was among the correspondents fired in the overhaul.

Disney's ABC submitted license renewal applications for its eight owned-and-operated TV stations to the Federal Communications Commission Thursday, but did so under protest. ABC said it believes the FCC order is unlawful, arbitrary and unconstitutional.

The FCC Media Bureau issued an order last month forcing ABC to reapply for spectrum licenses for its eight local stations. ABC called the order unprecedented.

In other entertainment news, a 21-year-old Austrian man was sentenced to 15 years in prison after pleading guilty to planning an attack at a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. Beran A. had planned to assault concertgoers with knives and bombs. The man was found guilty of planning the attack and other terrorism-related offenses.

The Commodores announced they will not perform at the Freedom 250 concert series scheduled for Washington, D.C. next month. The group joins Morris Day and Young MC in exiting the lineup. The departures followed backlash from fans after the concerts were announced Wednesday morning over ties to Trump.

A Google employee allegedly used insider data to win an online bet that D4vd would be the most searched artist of 2025. Federal authorities say the man pocketed $1.2 million from Polymarket trades based on confidential information.

cards.headline: Austrian Man Sentenced to 15 Years for Plotting Taylor Swift Concert Attack
cards.teaser: A 21-year-old received prison time after pleading guilty to planning an assault with knives and bombs at a Vienna concert.
cards.body:
A 21-year-old Austrian man has been sentenced to 15 years in prison after being found guilty of planning an attack at a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. He pleaded guilty to terrorism-related offences connected to the plot.

The concert was scheduled to take place in Vienna before authorities uncovered the scheme and prevented it from proceeding.

cards.headline: Google Employee Accused of Using Insider Data to Win $1.2 Million Bet
cards.teaser: Federal authorities say a Google staffer used confidential information to place winning bets on Polymarket about the most searched artist of 2025.
cards.body:
A Google software engineer has been charged with using confidential company information to make profitable trades on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. Michele Spagnuolo, 36, allegedly leveraged access to Google's search data through his position to place bets on which artists would top the company's most-searched lists, earning $1.2 million in profits.

The US Department of Justice unsealed the complaint against Spagnuolo in February. His case follows similar charges against a US Army soldier who was accused of using classified information to place bets on Polymarket regarding military operations.

cards.headline: The Commodores Exit Freedom 250 Concert Series After Trump Backlash
cards.teaser: The group joins Morris Day and Young MC in dropping out of the Washington, D.C. shows following fan criticism over Trump ties.
cards.body:
The Commodores announced they will not perform at the Freedom 250 concert series scheduled for Washington, D.C. next month. The group is the latest act to exit the lineup, following departures by Morris Day and Young MC.

The exits followed quick backlash from fans after the concerts were announced Wednesday morning. Fans criticized the retro-heavy bill over its ties to Trump, prompting the artists to withdraw from the shows.

cards.headline: Scooter Braun Discusses Taylor Swift, Kanye West in New Interview
cards.teaser: The former music manager sat for a 90-minute podcast conversation covering his relationships with major artists.
cards.body:
Scooter Braun, former manager to Justin Bieber, Ariana Grande and Kanye West, participated in a 90-minute interview with Suzy Weiss for her Second Thought podcast, released Thursday. The conversation marks one of Braun's rare public appearances since stepping down as CEO of Hybe America and retiring from management.

During the interview, Braun discussed his work with Taylor Swift and Kanye West, along with artists Spencer Pratt and Sydney Sweeney.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Announces Season 8 Cast Including Paralympic Athlete
cards.teaser: The lineup features 12 new contestants, including the brother of a Season 7 cast member and a bronze medal winner.
cards.body:
Love Island USA has revealed the Season 8 cast, featuring 12 new contestants entering the villa. Notable islanders include Zach Georgiou, whose brother Charlie competed in Season 7, and Beatriz Hatz, a Paralympic athlete and bronze medal winner.

The season premieres June 2 with daily episodes during premiere week, followed by a regular episode schedule.

cards.headline: ABC Submits FCC License Renewals Under Protest
cards.teaser: Disney's ABC filed required applications for its eight local stations while calling the agency order unlawful and unconstitutional.
cards.body:
Disney's ABC submitted license renewal applications for its eight owned-and-operated TV stations to the Federal Communications Commission as ordered, but filed under protest. The broadcaster stated that the FCC's order is unlawful, arbitrary, and unconstitutional.

The FCC Media Bureau issued the order last month, requiring ABC to reapply for spectrum licenses for its eight local stations. ABC characterized the directive as unprecedented.

hero.headline: Justice Department investigates Reid Hoffman nonprofit over E. Jean Carroll legal funding
hero.body:
The Department of Justice has opened an investigation into a nonprofit organization run by billionaire Reid Hoffman, examining contributions that partially funded legal expenses for E. Jean Carroll during her civil lawsuit against President Trump, according to a source familiar with the matter.

Hoffman, who co-founded LinkedIn, has donated millions of dollars to Democratic causes and the party over multiple years. He has been a vocal critic of Trump for an extended period.

The investigation has raised questions about whether it represents retaliation against Trump critics. It also tests the independence of Department of Justice officials in handling cases involving the president's political opponents.

Carroll successfully sued Trump in civil court over allegations of sexual assault. Two juries decided the case in her favor, awarding her millions of dollars in damages. The legal proceedings concluded before this investigation began.

The nonprofit investigation focuses specifically on how Hoffman's organization distributed funds and whether any of those contributions improperly supported Carroll's lawsuit expenses. The exact legal basis for the investigation has not been disclosed publicly.

Hoffman's financial support for Democratic candidates and progressive causes spans many years. His philanthropic work has touched numerous political and social issues beyond this specific legal matter.

Hosts of the ABC program The View criticized the investigation on Thursday, questioning why the administration would spend resources relitigating a case that juries had already resolved. The criticism reflects broader concerns among Trump critics about potential political motivations behind the probe.

The investigation marks another instance where the Justice Department under the current administration has scrutinized individuals and organizations connected to legal actions against Trump. The outcome of the probe remains uncertain, and no charges have been filed.

cards.headline: Trump administration opens Ebola quarantine facility in Kenya for exposed Americans
cards.teaser: A 50-bed field hospital in Kenya will house Americans exposed to Ebola, with no plans to allow them back into the United States.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is establishing a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola during the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rather than allowing them to return to the United States. The 50-bed field hospital will become operational Friday.

The policy shift has drawn criticism from some experts, who argue that preventing Americans from returning home may hinder treatment efforts.

cards.headline: Police respond to swatting call at Supreme Court Justice Amy Coney Barrett's home
cards.teaser: Law enforcement received a false report of gunshots at Barrett's Virginia residence.
cards.body:
Supreme Court Justice Amy Coney Barrett's Virginia home was targeted by a swatting call on Wednesday night. Law enforcement received a report of gunshots at her suburban address in Fairfax County.

Dispatchers alerted responding officers that a high-priority county resident lived at the location, suggesting the report might not be legitimate. Fairfax County police confirmed the incident occurred.

cards.headline: Court orders Customs chief to testify on tariff refunds process
cards.teaser: Customs and Border Protection Commissioner Rodney Scott must appear at a June hearing in New York.
cards.body:
The U.S. Court of International Trade ordered Customs and Border Protection Commissioner Rodney Scott to appear at a hearing next month to testify about the Trump administration's tariff refunds process. The hearing will take place in New York on June 9.

The court issued the order Wednesday, requiring Scott to provide testimony about how the refund process is being implemented. The tariff refunds program has been a subject of legal scrutiny as importers and businesses seek clarity on the administration's trade policies.

cards.headline: Treasury Department prepares $250 bill featuring Trump
cards.teaser: The Bureau of Engraving and Printing is designing the new bill, which requires congressional approval to print.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is pushing Congress to approve a $250 bill bearing President Trump's portrait, according to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The proposal would require changing federal law, which currently prohibits any living person from appearing on US currency. Bessent stated the bill would celebrate the country's 250th anniversary of independence, and the Treasury has already begun preparing designs.

Democrats have vowed to block the move. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries responded sharply on social media, calling himself "a hard no" on the proposal and telling Trump to "get over yourself." Congressional approval is required before any new currency can be printed and distributed.

cards.headline: Michigan Democrats clash over campaign donations in Senate debate
cards.teaser: Three candidates vying to replace retiring Senator Gary Peters debated foreign and corporate funding.
cards.body:
Representative Haley Stevens, state Senator Mallory McMorrow, and Abdul El-Sayed faced off in a contentious Thursday debate as they compete in Michigan's Democratic primary to succeed retiring Senator Gary Peters.

The candidates sparred over their approaches to campaign finance, with foreign and corporate donations emerging as a key point of contention during the exchange. The August primary race is expected to be competitive.

cards.headline: Los Angeles mayoral race features former reality TV star as serious contender
cards.teaser: Mayor Karen Bass faces 15 challengers including Spencer Pratt in a nonpartisan primary.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles mayoral race has drawn national attention as it transformed from a local contest into one of the more unconventional municipal races in recent memory. Mayor Karen Bass faces a challenge from 15 candidates, including former reality TV star Spencer Pratt, whose candidacy has moved from novelty to serious contender.

The nonpartisan primary takes place Tuesday and will determine which candidates advance to the general election. The race has generated viral moments as candidates compete for attention in the nation's second-largest city.
